title: Surgically produced, controllable immunocompromised pigs
protocol: Sedate the pig with midazolam (0.3 mg/kg, i.m.) and atropine (0.04 mg/kg, i.m.).
Wait until the pig is completely calm.
Administer buprenorphine (0.01~0.02 mg/kg, i.m.) for 30 min before the start of surgery.
In the surgical preparation room, shave the puncture site under inhaled isoflurane with 2 liter/min oxygen via a face mask.
Insert a 22-gauge angiocatheter into posterior auricular vein to access i.v. and place a secure airway.
Perform endotracheal intubation with a 6.5- to 7.5-mm tube for airway protection.
After shaving, move the pig to the operating room.
Place the pig in the supine position.
Deliver ongoing maintenance anesthesia with 1–2% isoflurane through a nose cone.
Monitor pulse oximetry, body temperature, and heart rate throughout anesthesia induction, maintenance, and recovery.
Disinfect the operation area.
Use sterile surgical instruments.
Perform incision of the skin on the upper manubrium of the sternum from near the midline neck hyoid bone (approximately 7 cm).
Dissect subcutaneous tissue while avoiding the carotid artery and vagus nerve on both sides of the sternohyoid muscle.
Pinch the ends of the thymus on both sides of the sternohyoid muscle with forceps.
When dissecting the thymus and subcutaneous tissue, perform dissection to the back of the manubrium of the sternum.
Pass the right cervical lobe under the anterior neck muscles to enable traction to be applied on both the left and right cervical lobes simultaneously.
Apply traction to pull the left and right cervical lobes to the cranial side.
Carefully dissect and remove the thoracic lobe in the anterior mediastinum.
Suture the subcutaneous tissue and skin after thymectomy.
Perform a midline incision from the region proximal to the xiphoid process to the lower abdomen for splenectomy.
Incise the muscle layer using a scalpel for splenectomy.
Incise the peritoneum using an electric scalpel for splenectomy.
Secure the field of view in the perisplenic region by using a retractor for splenectomy.
Lift the spleen to expose the three blood vessels: splenic body omental vessels, short gastric vessels, and the splenic vessels.
Dissect the renal fascia before lifting the spleen to easily visualize the three blood vessels.
Ligate the splenic artery and short gastric artery at one place on the splenic side for splenectomy.
Ligate two places on the abdominal side of the arteries for splenectomy.
Resect the section between the ligation points after ligating the arteries.
Dissect the part away from the ligation position to prevent hemorrhage for splenectomy.
Remove the spleen after performing vessel dissection for splenectomy.
Attach a gastric fistula tube after splenectomy.
Prepare an intravenous tube with about 1/3 of the drip chamber remaining.
Secure a field of view of the region surrounding the short stomach artery ligature of the stomach.
Put a thread around the planned incision site on the upper part on the side of the greater curvature of the stomach for performing purse-string suturing.
Using an electric scalpel, make a 1 to 1.5 cm incision required for gastrostomy tube insertion.
Insert the drip chamber side of the processed gastrostomy tube into the stomach.
Perform purse-string suture to prevent the tube from coming out of the stomach.
Fasten tube to stomach by Witzel sutures.
The tip of the gastrostomy tube is pulled out from the region surrounding the costal arch.
Join the fixed parts of the stomach tube with the abdominal wall at 4 to 5 places by 3-0 nylon thread.
Fix the opening of the subcutaneous tissue of the back with 4-0 nylon thread.
Reconstitute tacrolimus tablets in hot water at 50 to 60°C to create a 25 mg/mL solution.
Prepare Prednisolone as a 5 mg/mL solution in the same manner as tacrolimus.
Dissolve CELLCEPT powder for oral suspension in water to prepare mycophenolate mofetil (MMF).
Adjust the administration volume according to the administration dose.
Push the jelly filled in the tube into the stomach using 30 mL of heated water.
Administer immunosuppressant.
Push any remaining immunosuppressant in the tube into the stomach using 30 mL of heated water.
Fill the gastrostomy tube with 30 mL of PG water.
Thaw serum and heat-inactivate for 30 min at 56 ℃.
Store heat-inactivated serum in 50-mL aliquots at -20 ℃.
Supplement RPMI-1640 with 10% (vol/vol) FBS and 1% (vol/vol) penicillin-streptomycin for culturing PBMC derived from MMP peripheral blood.
Store the supplemented medium at 4 ℃ and warm to room temperature before use.
Dissolve PHA powder in PBS to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Suspend 10 mg of powder in 10 mL of PBS to make a 1 mg/mL stock solution.
Store the stock solution in aliquots at -20°C for several months.
Transfer 100 mL of CellTiter-Glo buffer into an amber bottle containing CellTiter-Glo substrate.
Mix the reagent by gently vortexing.
Store the reconstituted reagent in aliquots at -20°C for several months.
Optimize the assay system for PBMC proliferation studies.
Examine cell density ranging from 1 × 10^4 cells to 2 × 10^5 cells per well.
Test stimulant (PHA) concentrations between 0.1 and 10 μg/mL.
Determine optimal incubation time between 48 and 96 hours.
Observe sub-maximum proliferative activity at a cell density of 5 × 10^4 cells/well in 96 well round bottom plate with 3 μg/mL PHA after 72 h incubation.
Collect approximately 7 mL of blood from male micro mini-pig using a sodium heparinized 10-ml syringe.
Transfer 5 mL of fresh blood into 15-mL conical tubes containing 5 mL of PBS.
Gently mix by drawing the blood and buffer in and out of a pipette.
Aliquot 5 mL of Ficoll-Paque PLUS into two 15-mL conical tubes.
Place the tip of the pipette against inside of the tube, carefully layer 5 mL of diluted blood onto the 5 mL of Ficoll-Paque PLUS already filled.
Centrifuge the tubes at 400 g for 30 min at room temperature.
Using a clean pipette, carefully collect the white layer of PBMC between plasma and Ficoll-Paque PLUS.
Transfer the cells to a clean 50 mL centrifuge tube containing 20 mL of RPMI-1640.
After gentle pipetting, centrifuge the tubes at 400 g for 10 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells thoroughly in 20 mL RPMI-1640 by pipetting.
Count cells using a 1:2 dilution with trypan blue.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1400 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend cells in culture medium at a final concentration of 5 × 10^5 cells per mL.
Transfer 100 μL (5 × 10^4 cells) per well to a 96-well round-bottom plate.
Add 60 μL of culture media and 20 μL of 10-fold concentrated MPA to the cells.
Pre-incubate the cells for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Add 20 μL of 30 μg/mL PHA to the cells, achieving a final concentration of 3 μg/mL.
Incubate the cells for 3 days at 37°C.
Equilibrate the plate and its contents at room temperature for 30 min.
Remove 100 μL of culture media from each well.
Add 100 μL of CellTiter-Glo Reagent to each well.
Mix contents on an orbital shaker to induce cell lysis.
Allow the plate to incubate for 10 min at room temperature to stabilize luminescent signal.
Transfer 100 μL of cell lysate to opaque-walled multiwell plates.
Measure luminescence by microplate reader.
Perform catheterization surgery one week before pharmacokinetics study in male micro mini-pig.

Incise the skin and subcutaneous muscular layer 2-3 cm from the cervical ventral midline approximately 3 -4 cm to the head side along the body axis from approximately 2 cm from the anterior border of scapula to the sternum.
Dissect the internal jugular vein using artery forceps.
Ligate the blood vessels on the head side after dissection.
Thread catheter fixation thread in chest side blood vessel.
Insert CVC 5-8 cm into the vessel and perform fixation with a thread so that the catheter does not move.
Adjust the insertion depth of the catheter based on the size of the animal.
Inject 2 mL of heparinized saline from the end of the catheter and attach an injection cap after confirming that blood can be collected with a catheter.
Suture the muscular layer, subcutaneous tissue, and the incision in the skin.
Attach the clip at approximately 1 cm from the incision to the catheter coming out of the body through the incision on the skin.
Fixate the clip by suturing it onto the skin.
Store the jacket pocket from the clip fixation part to the end part.
Prepare a CELLCEPT powder for oral suspension as mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) or use CELLCEPT Capsule 250 alternatively.
Administer the MMF suspension via gastrostomy.
Administer the morning dose of MMF at 20 mg/kg after 15 minutes following feeding.
Collect approximately 0.5 mL of blood from the central vein (CV) with a sodium heparinized syringe before dosing and at specified intervals after dosing: 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10, 12, and 24 hours.
Centrifuge blood samples at 1,200 x G for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Store isolated plasma at -20 to -30°C until analysis.
Measure the plasma concentration of mycophenolic acid by LC/MS/MS method.
